stickies.body:
The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds.

**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer's subject. **Skills** are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. **Processes** are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. **Tools** are what an agent can call.

Getting anything in is **acquisition**: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through `uploads/` or through the conversation, and are ingested into `library/`. It is a step rather than a graph typology of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for.

**Scope:** the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio's chapters.

directories.description: This instance's own reader-facing pages, and the page `/folio-assistant-core/` serves. Without a docs directory the harness tile can only open this instance's section of the landing (`/#harness-folio-assistant-core`), and `harness-tiles.ts` reports that as a finding. Authored markdown, composed THROUGH just-the-docs like the FHIR IG layers' pages, so it gets the sidebar, search and layout. Declared in this instance's own file, not in `cat-harness.json`: `compose-docs.docsLayers` treats every docs-kind entry there as a composition layer, so declaring it there would overlay this `index.md` onto the site's own.

The gettext side of folio-assistant-core's own strings, one directory per target locale: `block-kinds.pot`/`.po`, the headings of the block kinds this instance declares in block-kinds/, keyed `msgctxt "block-kind:<kind>"` with the node's English `heading` as msgid. Locale headings live in the translation graph, and kinds are not centrally managed, so the catalogue sits with the kinds rather than in cat-harness/translations/.

The document profile's block kinds (prose, example, remark, algorithm, simulator, equation, diagram, table, figure, recommendation), one folio-block-kind/v1 node per file. Kinds are discoverable and not centrally managed: cat-harness/schemas/block-kinds.ts finds these by scanning every instance's declared block-kinds graph.

The `document` block VOCABULARY's node, folio-content-adapter/v1: its name, its companion roles (md, ts) and that cat-harness's code types it. Every kind in block-kinds/ names it. Each layer declares its own adapter and a folio may mix them, so the paper profile is core's `document` kinds plus the science layer's `mathpaper` kinds.
The validators folio-assistant-core's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks.

Code lists this layer owns, one `folio-code-list/v1` file per list, inherited by every dependent through the dependency overlay (`codeListDirs`) and exported as SKOS with the harness's. A `recommendation` block's `strength` names a code here, so the check is "resolves in the scheme" rather than a closed enum. Two lists: `grade-recommendation-strength` (GRADE as WHO applies it) and `rfc2119-requirement-level` (BCP 14). A folio whose issuing body grades differently declares its own list rather than editing these.

The QA checkers this layer's code provides, one `folio-qa-checker/v1` node per criterion, registered for a folio through its dependency tree by `loadContributions`. Two: `recommendation-strength-resolves`, naming `RECOMMENDATION_CHECKERS` in `pipeline/qa-checkers-recommendation.ts`, and `acronym-in-glossary`, naming `ACRONYM_CHECKERS` in `pipeline/qa-checkers-acronyms.ts`. The criterion itself is declared in cat-harness-tools' QA registry with `checker_contributed`.

The generic pipeline slots this layer fills, one `folio-pipeline-plugin/v1` node per slot, naming `PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATIONS` in `pipeline/plugin-slots.ts`, registered for a folio through its dependency tree by `loadContributions`. One: `tabular-csvw`, through which cat-harness-tools' `ingest-document.ts` reaches this layer's CSVW extractors (`scripts/tabular-csv.ts`, `scripts/tabular-xlsx.ts`) without naming this layer.

`pipeline/qa-checkers-recommendation.ts` and `pipeline/qa-checkers-acronyms.ts`, the automated checkers `qa-checkers/recommendation-strength-resolves.json` and `qa-checkers/acronym-in-glossary.json` name (`RECOMMENDATION_CHECKERS`, `ACRONYM_CHECKERS`), and `pipeline/plugin-slots.ts`, the table `pipeline-plugins/tabular-csvw.json` names (`PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATIONS`). Under `pipeline/` because that is where the harness's `imports` input-site looks for a contributed checker, as for every layer.

The graph typologies folio-assistant-core owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file. There is no central registry for subgraph types; a harness declares its own in a kinds/ graph, each entry carrying its rationale.
The schemas of the content layer's Node Kinds.
directories._description_comment: The content layer's own schema nodes. Three today, and they are one chain: `dublin-core` is what a source system SAYS about an item, `catalogue` is the shape of the collection that item sits in, and `materialization` is whether any of its bytes are actually here. The third is the load-bearing one — see its module doc for why bootstrap fetching a harness and the IRIS catalogue instance fetching three items out of 361.55 GB are the same process with two names.

directories.description: What an AUTHOR creates using the graph -- a note, a visualization, a paper -- referencing the KG and rendered through the harness's just-the-docs document rendering. It declares the EXISTING `folio` kind rather than a new one: `folio` is 'authored content, rendered to a website', registered by core because only core can render it. The contrast is with `docs` in cat-harness, whose subject is the harness itself. Example: a catalogue goes in `library/` or is referenced remotely; a note ABOUT it is a folio; the page explaining how ingestion works is docs.

Core's glossary: folio-glossary/v1 documents, each a SKOS concept scheme of local terms linked to external SKOS concepts by exactMatch/closeMatch, plus external concepts listed as members without being copied. A whole external scheme is referenced through remoteGraphs with graphTypologies ["glossary"]. `dependents: reproduce` so every folio built on core gets its own glossary/. Rendered on the glossary/ page with the swimlane ledger (cat-harness's `swimlane-glossary`) as one more source; checked by `check:glossary`.

The content layer's Tool nodes, such as `folio-changeset`, which exposes `schemas/changeset.ts`. Reached by the harness through tool auto-discovery, never by an import: the harness may not import core, and a Tool node is a declaration loaded by path.

The content layer's own ContentAdapters: `document/`. Its imports into `cat-harness-tools/src/`, `cat-harness/schemas/` and `cat-harness-tools/pipeline/` are DOWNWARD and therefore legal (core declares `needs: ["cat-harness"]`); nothing in the harness imports it. Its consuming tests live in `scripts/tests/`. It needs `tsconfig.json`'s `include` entry (without it `bun run typecheck` passes while covering fewer files) and the `BUILTIN_ADAPTERS` module path, which is resolved by variable specifier, so no static-import gate checks it. `paper/` is the science layer's, in that layer's own `adapters/paper/`.

Core's own server half: the HTTP routes that act on a folio's CONTENT — `routes/feedback.ts` (its feedback items), `routes/glossary.ts` (its glossary candidates), `routes/relevance.ts` (its bibliography relevance). A content package's server half lives with its content. The server in `cat-harness-tools` declares them by their `src/routes/*` path and finds them here through `needs`, since core needs `cat-harness-tools`; they import the server's contract (`route-groups`, `types`, `core/rbac`) DOWN from it.

Core's own executable surface, with every test beside its subject: the review-comment Tool and its move helper, the glossary extractors and builder (`build-glossary.ts`, its `:refterm` codemod `codemod-refterm.ts`), the sample-import pair, the materialisation trio (`check-materialized-fixity`, `backfill-materialized-fixity`, `cache-index`), `check-voices.ts` (every voice rule's citation resolved through `schemas/library-ref.ts` into a folio's `library/`), `build-document-site.ts` (which reads `schemas/changeset.ts`), and the document, bibliography, public-comment and tabular tools. Pipeline scripts are addressed by id, and `resolvePipelineScript` searches the folio, then the platform, then here. Two scripts are invocation surfaces, named by path and so not to be moved without updating their callers: `build-document-site.ts`, which a DOCUMENT folio's generated staging workflow names (`init-folio.ts` writes `folio-assistant-core/scripts/build-document-site.ts` and `init-folio.test.ts` pins it), and `review-comments.ts`, invoked by path from `folio-staging.yml`.

Files this layer's tools WRITE INTO a folio that opts in, kept as real files rather than strings inside a script. `public-comment/github/` holds the issue forms and the two workflows that `scripts/public-comment-changesets.ts install` copies into a folio's `.github/` (`TEMPLATE_DIR`). They live here because this layer is the only one that installs them.

L1 source content this LAYER owns — the publications core's own vocabulary and methods are derived FROM, one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document. Declared rather than borrowed because a method is placed by OWNERSHIP (`methodology-adoption` §4): a paper core's methodology cites from another instance's library would not lift out with it. Holds Doc-Researcher (`arxiv-2510.21603v1`), the C2PA Technical Specification 2.5 (`c2pa-2026-specification-2-5`, CC-BY-4.0) and the DSpace 7 REST Contract (`dspace-7-rest-contract`, BSD-3-Clause). `ingest-document.ts` refuses to guess a destination when several are declared. `dependents: skip` because these are THIS layer's sources; a downstream folio's library is its own.

The methodologies core adopts from its own corpus. A method belongs to the layer whose job it describes, so the directory lifts out with this instance and nothing else moves. Core's job is what a folio HOLDS, where it CAME FROM and how much is PRESENT — which is why a document-ingestion method is core's and not the harness's.
The skills core owns, including `skills/voices/`: a voice partitions how prose READS and is a different graph from an instruction body.

The BPMN core owns, by area: `content/` (authoring, editing and HCI validation, draft to publication, the content lifecycle, change review, evidence retrieval, contributor feedback), `library/` (L1 document ingestion and `deep-document-research`, Doc-Researcher's iterative loop), `conduct/` (getting started) and `ui/` (board interactions), with their DMN tables in each area's `decisions/`. A TOP-LEVEL directory, as the harness's diagrams are: `check:layout-norms` refuses a package subdirectory of an already-declared graph such as `methodologies/processes/`, and `workflowDirs` resolves only from a DECLARED directory.

Scenarios: the roles an actor takes on, in `roles.json`, the user stories told as them, in `stories.json`, and the actors in `actors/` (deep-researcher, evidence-agent, onboarding-agent). This layer's `address-*` voices point at them, and `check:voices` reads this declaration to find the role graph.

What auditing THIS instance produced, kept so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean". Stored on the `qa-reports` branch keyed by commit (`storage`), not committed: a local run writes the working copy here and `.gitignore` keeps it out of the checkout (bean 7mwa) — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 7 files across processes (1), scenarios (1), skills (1), tools (4). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it. Since `storage` was added, a reader resolves it from the store rather than the checkout, so its absence on disk reads as `unknown`, not clean.

Agent memory about content authoring, review and publication: lessons (block kinds, the document render path, normative statements, locale directories) an agent carries between sessions, one `"$schema": "folio-memory/v1"` node each. Read by cat-harness's `agent-memory` assembler alongside every other instance's declared `memory` directory.
The work plan for folio-assistant-core.

GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, and a shim no node names. The kind is cat-harness's (one outside-software core shared with `tool-release`); this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions.

Repository health reports for THIS repository: the one `health-report/v1` document `bun run cat-harness-tools/test/health/run.ts --instance <this instance>` writes. Each repository the separation made is its own clone, with its own size, publish branch, branches and stores, so each carries its own report (owner, 2026-10-10: "All repos need health check"). The graph typology is cat-harness's; its `health` entry says what separates a health report (about the repository) from a `qa` verdict (about an artefact).
